answer: A jade marketplace can stop aliases from multiplying voting power by weighting votes with locked deposits rather than account counts. Set a fixed horizon for withdrawals before proposals are announced, so attackers cannot borrow a deposit briefly, vote, and return it immediately. Splitting one deposit across identities preserves its total weight; to forge majority influence, an attacker must immobilize more capital for the full lock period. This resists cheap identities but favors wealthy holders and cannot eliminate bribery.
